state.case_summary:
A 33-year-old woman with no prior health issues was admitted to the acute medical care unit after experiencing two days of lethargy and general malaise. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She reported severe, continuous pain in her right upper limb, which was not influenced by any specific factors, and severe weakness in the same limb. She had three episodes of vomiting and diarrhea and had been taking paracetamol for flu-like symptoms for three days as prescribed by her general practitioner. On the morning of her admission, she noticed swelling in her lips and tongue and experienced shortness of breath. Ambulance staff administered intramuscular adrenaline due to a threatened airway, and she was transported to the acute medical unit for further care. Upon admission, her pulse rate was 110/min, respiratory rate was 22/min, and she had a fever with a temperature of 38.9°C. She was agitated, restless, and incontinent. Three hours later, she developed facial swelling. The facial skin remained intact without erythema, rash, or blisters. Examination of her oral cavity showed an oedematous tongue, pharynx, and buccal mucosa without any detectable septic focus. There was no neck stiffness or localizing neurological signs, and her Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score was 14. Examination of the head and neck revealed no local rise in temperature, no tenderness, no palpable lymph nodes, and no surgical emphysema. Air entry was equal on both sides, but diffusely scattered rhonchi were present. Cardiovascular examination was normal. Abdominal examination showed localized tenderness in the left iliac fossa. Pelvic and perineal examination by a gynecologist was normal. Examination of the right upper limb showed no soft tissue or skeletal injuries, no signs of cellulitis, erythema, or blisters. Soft tissue palpation was non-tender, with no signs of grimacing or withdrawal, and the consistency was soft with no signs of compartment syndrome. Active movements at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints were within normal range and painless. All peripheral pulses were normal with satisfactory capillary circulation.

A repeat blood culture at 48 hours following admission was positive for alpha haemolytic (viridans) streptococcus mitis.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

severe weakness in right upper limb

alarm_features: septic features with fever and positive blood culture
